---
title: "💻 Command line"
---

Every command is run as `krsim <command>`, and `krsim <command> --help` lists all of its options. The examples use seed `42` and write to `results/`.

## Main pipeline

::: {.stage}
### 🦟 Stage 1 — Simulate genealogy

```bash
krsim simulate \
    --Nh 100 --T 50 --K 2 --chi 0.18 --C 1 \
    --recombination_rate 7.4e-7 \
    --random_seed 42 \
    --output_dir results/ \
    --save_pairs
```

Always writes the tree sequence `ts_{seed}.trees`, which every later stage starts from, and the individual–node mapping `sim_ind_node_map_{seed}.csv` (which strains each host carries, with each node's `time` in generations before present; `0` = most recent/current generation), needed by `vcf-host-depth` and `relate-host`. The `--save_*` flags below add extra outputs.

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--Nh` | Number of human hosts |
| `--T` | Transmission generations |
| `--K` | Parasites transmitted per mosquito bite |
| `--chi` | Superinfection probability (0–1) |
| `--C` | Oocysts per mosquito |
| `--recombination_rate` | Per-bp recombination rate — uses `7.4e-7` (*P. falciparum*) if not given |
| `--random_seed` | Seed for reproducibility |
| `--output_dir` | Output directory |
| `--save_pairs` | Save recombinant node pairs to `node_pairs_{seed}.csv` |
| `--save_lineage` | Save per-generation child→parent strain lineage to `lineage_{seed}.csv`, plus a `node_id_map_{seed}.csv` pre/post-`simplify()` ID mapping — turn this on if you want true generation-by-generation parentage (for `krsim strain-transmission-map`, `krsim pairwise-strain-pedigree-map`, or your own pedigree analysis), since the final tree sequence alone can skip generations |
:::

::: {.stage}
### ⚡ Stage 2 — Add mutations

```bash
krsim mutate \
    --ts results/ts_42.trees \
    --mutation_rate 1e-6 \
    --random_seed 42 \
    --output_dir results/
```

If `--mutation_rate` is not given, `1e-6` per bp is used. Outputs `ts_mut_{seed}.trees`. All stages from here onwards use the mutated tree sequence.
:::

::: {.stage}
### ⏳ Stage 3 — Coalescence & mutation times

```bash
krsim coal-mut \
    --ts results/ts_mut_42.trees \
    --random_seed 42 \
    --output_dir results/
```

Outputs `coal_T_{seed}.csv` (pairwise MRCA times per tree interval) and `mut_T_{seed}.csv` (position and age of every mutation). Both tables include a `chromosome` column (1-indexed, from `krsim/sim/params.py`'s `COMP_BREAKPOINTS`), with `position`/`left`/`right` given as chromosome-local coordinates rather than genome-wide ones. `coal_T` only contains rows where the sample pair has a common ancestor in that tree interval — pairs with no shared ancestry anywhere in the ARG are simply absent from the table.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Small runs only
`coal_T` has one row for every pair of strains in every tree, so it is easy to read for a small run like the [quick start](quickstart.qmd), but very computationally expensive for larger populations. See [Running at scale](scaling.qmd#coal-mut-is-for-small-runs).
:::
:::

::: {.stage}
### 🧬 Stage 4 — Strain-level VCF

```bash
krsim vcf-strain \
    --ts results/ts_mut_42.trees \
    --random_seed 42 \
    --output_dir results/
```

Outputs `output_{seed}_strain.vcf` — one sample column per parasite strain (node), genotypes `0`/`1`.
:::

::: {.stage}
### 🧍 Stage 5 — Host-level VCF

```bash
# depth from real depth files
krsim vcf-host-depth \
    --strain_vcf results/output_42_strain.vcf \
    --ind_node_map_csv results/sim_ind_node_map_42.csv \
    --depth_zip my_depth.zip \
    --random_seed 42 \
    --output_dir results/

# or modelled depth, no data needed
krsim vcf-host-depth \
    --strain_vcf results/output_42_strain.vcf \
    --ind_node_map_csv results/sim_ind_node_map_42.csv \
    --depth_model sWGA \
    --random_seed 42 \
    --output_dir results/
```

Mixes each host's strains the way sequencing a blood sample would, with realistic read depth that varies along the genome as in real data (see [realistic read depth](realistic-depth.qmd)). Give one depth source:

- **`--depth_zip FILE`:** a zip of `<sample>.window_stats.tsv` depth files (mean and SD of depth in every 500 bp window), made from your own samples with [`krsim depth-zip`](#helper-depth-zip), or an example zip of 100 sWGA or 100 gDNA Pf8 samples. The files must come from reads mapped to the 3D7 reference used by MalariaGEN Pf8 (PlasmoDB-54); krsim checks every file it uses and stops if one doesn't match. The zip needs at least one file per host. If it has more, files are picked at random, each used at most once, set by `--random_seed`.
- **`--depth_model sWGA|gDNA`:** depth simulated from a model fitted to Pf8: AR(8) for sWGA, ARMA(2,2) for gDNA, both with Student t kicks. Optional:
  - `--depth_mean X`: centre of the hosts' typical depths
  - `--depth_spread S`: how much hosts' typical depths differ (SD of log depth); `0` gives every host `--depth_mean`, though depth still varies along each host's genome
  - `--depth_params FILE`: a JSON file changing any other model value, e.g. `{"nu": 3.0, "cap": 1000}`; values not listed keep their defaults. The settings are `ar`, `ma`, `mu`, `scale`, `nu`, `offset`, `cap`, `end_width`, `end_factor`, `depth_mean` and `depth_spread`; `krsim vcf-host-depth --help` lists the defaults

::: {.callout-note}
## Flat depth, for testing
For an idealised control with no depth variation, use `--depth_spread 0` (every host the same typical depth) with `--depth_params` set to `{"scale": 0, "end_width": 0}` (no variation along the genome, and no low-depth sWGA chromosome ends). Each site's read count is still a Poisson draw, so a site can occasionally get 0 reads. This isn't realistic, but it lets you test a method without the effect of uneven depth.
:::

The model:

1. Within-host strain proportions sampled once per host from Dirichlet(α=1 per strain)
2. Each host's depth along the genome:
   - with `--depth_zip`: its depth file's mean *m* and SD *s* in each window
   - with `--depth_model`: a typical depth drawn once per host from a log-normal, times the host's own relative depth track from the model, capped at `cap` times the typical depth and, for sWGA, lowered near chromosome ends
3. At each variant site, the host's depth is drawn for the site's window:
   - with `--depth_zip`: a negative binomial with mean *m* and SD *s* (*r* = *m*² / (*s*² − *m*), *p* = *r* / (*r* + *m*)), since real read depth varies more than a Poisson; Poisson(*m*) if *s*² ≤ *m*; 0 if *m* = 0
   - with `--depth_model`: Poisson around the window's depth
4. The depth is split between the host's strains via Multinomial from the proportions
5. Reads are counted by allele and written as `GT:AD:DP`: `0/0` when all reads carry the ref allele, `1/1` when all carry the alt, `0/1` when both are seen (a mixed infection), and `./.` where the depth is 0. At a multi-allelic site (more than one ALT allele, from recurrent mutation), `AD` gives the reads for every allele and `GT` lists the two alleles with the most reads (e.g. `1/2`)

Outputs `output_{seed}_host_depth.vcf` (its header records the depth source and, for `--depth_model`, every value used), `host_depth_profiles_{seed}.csv` (each host's depth file, or its typical depth) and `host_depth_proportions_{seed}.csv`.
:::

::: {.stage}
### 🧰 Helper — zip of depth files {#helper-depth-zip}

```bash
krsim depth-zip \
    --bed sample1.per-base.bed.gz sample2.per-base.bed.gz \
    --output my_depth.zip
```

Not a pipeline step: it prepares the input for `vcf-host-depth --depth_zip`. It turns each sample's [mosdepth](https://github.com/brentp/mosdepth) per-base output (`<sample>.per-base.bed.gz`) into a depth file (`<sample>.window_stats.tsv`: mean and SD of depth in every 500 bp window) and puts them all in one zip. Each file is checked against the 3D7 reference used by Pf8. It takes a few seconds per sample.
:::

## Pedigree visualizations

Both maps need Stage 1 run with `--save_lineage`; the transmission map also needs the mutated tree sequence from Stage 2. See them in action in the [tutorial](quickstart.qmd#visualise-transmission).

::: {.stage}
### Strain transmission map — visualize the pedigree

```bash
krsim strain-transmission-map \
    --lineage_csv results/lineage_42.csv \
    --node_id_map_csv results/node_id_map_42.csv \
    --ts results/ts_mut_42.trees \
    --random_seed 42 \
    --output_dir results/
```

Needs `--save_lineage` from Stage 1 and `ts_mut_{seed}.trees` from Stage 2. Renders an interactive, self-contained `strain_transmission_map_{seed}.html` — a generation-by-generation pedigree diagram (founders at top, current samples at bottom, one lane per host) built from the pre-simplify `lineage_{seed}.csv`, so it shows the true parentage that `simplify()` compresses away. Each strain is labeled with its pre-simplify ID (with its post-simplify ID as a small corner badge, where one exists); clicking a strain traces and highlights its full ancestry and descendants. Every mutation is drawn as a × on the pedigree link, and at the time, where it happened. Pick a chromosome and a tree to fade out everything except the genealogy of that stretch of genome and its mutations. Open the file directly in a browser — no server or dependencies needed. Intended for small debug runs (a handful of hosts, a few dozen generations); it warns in-page and degrades gracefully past that, but isn't meant for production-scale runs (`--Nh 100`, etc.).
:::

::: {.stage}
### Pairwise strain pedigree map — trace two strains back to their shared ancestor

```bash
krsim pairwise-strain-pedigree-map \
    --lineage_csv results/lineage_42.csv \
    --node_id_map_csv results/node_id_map_42.csv \
    --random_seed 42 \
    --output_dir results/
```

Also only needs `--save_lineage` from Stage 1 — same inputs as the transmission map. Renders `pairwise_strain_pedigree_map_{seed}.html`: pick any two current-generation strains (dropdowns, or click two strains in the diagram) and it traces each one's full ancestry back through the pedigree, drawing strain 1's lineage in one color and strain 2's in another. Where the two colors overlap is a shared ancestor; the *most recent* shared ancestor(s) are highlighted as the coalescence point(s), with the number of generations back reported for each strain. Because a strain can have up to two immediate parents (one per gamete in the oocyst that produced it), there can be more than one coalescence point — the two ancestries can independently merge via more than one path.

This is a **pedigree** trace, not a genomic one: a shared ancestor here means the two strains' host lineages shared a parasite at that generation, not that any specific genomic region was actually inherited from it — recombination can replace a segment with DNA from the other parent at every step. Same small-debug-run scope as the transmission map.
:::

## Relatedness statistics

Optional ground-truth relatedness, computed from Stage 3's `coal_T` table. Not part of the tutorial — run these when you need true IBD.

```bash
krsim relate-strain \
    --coal_csv results/coal_T_42.csv \
    --random_seed 42 \
    --time_boundary 2 \
    --output_dir results/

krsim relate-host \
    --relate_csv results/relate_strain_42.csv \
    --ind_node_map_csv results/sim_ind_node_map_42.csv \
    --random_seed 42 \
    --output_dir results/
```

`krsim relate-strain`: for each strain pair in `coal_T_{seed}.csv`, sums the length of tree intervals where `coal_time <= --time_boundary` and divides by `GENOME_LENGTH` to give the fraction of the genome that is IBD below that time threshold. Pairs with no recorded coalescence anywhere in the ARG are not written as a row (rather than a `0` row). Outputs `relate_strain_{seed}.csv` (`sample_1`, `sample_2`, `frac_IBD`).

`krsim relate-host`: for each currently-infected host (from `sim_ind_node_map_{seed}.csv`, restricted to `time == 0`, i.e. the most recent generation), takes every pairwise combination of that host's strain nodes and averages their `frac_IBD` from `relate_strain_{seed}.csv`. Pairs missing from that table (no recorded coalescence) are treated as `frac_IBD = 0`. Hosts with fewer than two strains get an empty average. Outputs `relate_host_{seed}.csv` (`host`, `avg_frac_IBD`).
